land.text: the Uzbek SSR: 'On 27 October 1924, the Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic was created', with the autonomous republic of Karakalpakstan inside it

predecessors.note: 'On 31 August 1991, Uzbekistan declared independence after the failed coup attempt in Moscow.' 'The Soviet Union was dissolved on 26 December of that year.' Cliopatria's row starts in 1992; the USSR's last shape runs to 1991.

capitals.name: Tashkent
capitals.note: Infobox Tashkent 41°19′N 69°16′E; also the Uzbek SSR's capital.

rulers.name: Islam Karimov
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Elected as the first President of Uzbekistan on 29 December 1991'; died 2 September 2016.

rulers.name: Shavkat Mirziyoyev
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: In September 2016 'the Oliy Majlis appointed Prime Minister Shavkat Mirziyoyev as interim president'; 'In the December 2016 presidential election, Mirziyoyev was officially elected with 88.6% of the vote' and was sworn in on 14 December.

correction.text: the Uzbek SSR's territory, independent from 31 August 1991

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: independence was declared on 31 August 1991, four months before the Soviet Union 'was dissolved on 26 December'; Cliopatria's row starts in 1992. The 1992 outline is used for 1991 and overlaps the USSR's last year.

414,068 km2 against the infobox 448,978 km2 (4.9% water): ratio 0.92. On the grid the outline has 1,402 cells; 35 of them lie outside Natural Earth's Uzbekistan (17 in Kazakhstan, 5 in Turkmenistan, the rest elsewhere) and about 146 of Natural Earth's Uzbek cells are left out, 119 of them in Karakalpakstan; the page gives no figure to settle which line is right, so the outline stands. The frontiers are the Soviet republic lines of 1924-1929; the pages opened record no change of them in 1992-1995.
413,976 km2: identical to the 1992 outline on the grid (0 cells differ). No border event falls in 1996-1999 on the pages opened.

414,349 km2: one more grid cell than 1996 (+253 km2 at 59.8E 44.3N, Karakalpakstan). The page puts the Aral Sea retreat in these years ('In 1987, the lake split into two separate bodies of water'; 'it became first a peninsula in mid-2001'), so the added cell is read as a shoreline, not a frontier move; the ledger carries it as a gain from nobody at confidence 1.

415,143 km2 for 2006-2023: five more grid cells than 2000 (+1,264 km2, at 58.7-60.4E 44.5-44.9N in Karakalpakstan) and nothing else. The Aral page: 'In 2003, the South Aral further divided into eastern and western basins'; 'By 2007, it had declined to 10% of its original size'. The step is a shoreline, not a frontier. The Nov 2022 transfer of 156 km2 to Kyrgyzstan is below one grid cell (253 km2) and does not show.

Identical to 2006 on the grid. The page says 'Barak, a Kyrgyz enclave, existed in Uzbekistan until 2024'; an enclave that small does not show on the grid. The Uzbek enclaves in Kyrgyzstan (Sokh, Shohimardon, Chon-Kara/Qalacha) are drawn inside Kyrgyzstan's outline by the neighbour's shape, not here.

region.text: the Uzbek SSR within its Soviet borders, including Karakalpakstan; capital Tashkent

ledger.note: 31 August 1991: Uzbekistan declares independence from the USSR. 'On 31 August 1991, Uzbekistan declared independence after the failed coup attempt in Moscow'; 1 September became National Independence Day. The Soviet Union was dissolved on 26 December 1991.

region.text: one grid cell of Karakalpakstan at about 59.8E 44.3N that Cliopatria adds in 2000: the shore of the Aral Sea as it recedes

ledger.note: 2000: the receding Aral Sea leaves another strip of Karakalpakstan dry. Bridging entry: the shape steps by one cell; the Aral page gives 1987 (split into two), mid-2001 (Vozrozhdeniya Island a peninsula) and 2004 (17,160 km2, 25% of the original) but no year-by-year shoreline, so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Bagys area, 517 hectares of mountainous pastures

ledger.note: 2002: Bagys goes to Kazakhstan in the border settlement. 'Ultimately, Bagys was integrated into Kazakhstan'; 'An exchange of 517 hectares of mountainous pastures in the Bagys area for semi-desert lands near the villages of Nysan-1, Nysan-2, and Baimurat in the Kyzylorda Region helped finalize the agreement'; the Treaty on Specific Border Sections of 9 September 2002 completed the delimitation (in force 5 September 2003). The page does not say which side received which exchanged land, nor when Bagys changed hands; under 6 km2, below the grid.

region.text: five grid cells of Karakalpakstan at 58.7-60.4E 44.5-44.9N that Cliopatria adds in 2006: the Aral Sea shore

ledger.note: 2006: the shrinking South Aral leaves more of Karakalpakstan dry. Bridging entry: 'In 2003, the South Aral further divided into eastern and western basins'; 'By 2007, it had declined to 10% of its original size'. The page gives no area for 2006; the year is Cliopatria's. Kazakhstan's northern Aral shore moves in the same years (its dossier, kazakhstan_1996 and _2006).

region.text: 156 km2 along the Kyrgyz-Uzbek frontier; the page names no place

ledger.note: 17 November 2022: Uzbekistan cedes 156 km2 to Kyrgyzstan in the final border treaty. 'On November 17, 2022, Kyrgyzstan gained 156 km2 from Uzbekistan.' The page does not name the land (nor the Kempir-Abad reservoir, which it does not mention). Below one grid cell; the Kyrgyzstan dossier does not carry the matching gain.

region.text: the Kyrgyz enclave of Barak, which 'existed in Uzbekistan until 2024'

ledger.note: 2024: the Kyrgyz enclave of Barak inside Uzbekistan ends. 'Barak, a Kyrgyz enclave, existed in Uzbekistan until 2024.' The page gives no treaty, area or month and does not say the land passed to Uzbekistan (read from the enclave's ending); tiny, below the grid.

certainty.note: The frontiers are the Soviet republic lines of 1924-1929 (Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan page: the border 'assumed its current position in 1929'); the Kyrgyz and Tajik stretches were not yet delimited by treaty, and in 1999-2000 Uzbekistan began 'unilaterally demarcating and mining' them.

Kazakhstan: treaties of 16 November 2001 and 9 September 2002 (in force 2003); Kyrgyzstan: final treaty of November 2022; Tajikistan: 'landmark border deals' of 2018 whose terms the page does not give. The exception is the Aral Sea shore in Karakalpakstan, which retreats throughout and is soft.

sources.title: Uzbekistan
sources.note: Independence 31 August 1991, Uzbek SSR 27 October 1924, area 448,978 km2, capital, presidents. Silent on border treaties and Karakalpakstan's status.

sources.title: Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan border
sources.note: Treaties of 2001-2003, the Bagys exchange of 517 hectares, 1956 and 1963 Soviet-era transfers, the 128 km segment through the Aral Sea.

sources.title: Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan border
sources.note: Enclaves, the final treaty of November 2022 and the 156 km2 gained by Kyrgyzstan on 17 November 2022; Barak enclave until 2024. No areas for the enclaves.

sources.title: Tajikistan–Uzbekistan border
sources.note: Thin: 1924-1929 delimitation, 1999 mining, 2018 deals named by title only; no land swap, area or date on the page.

sources.title: Aral Sea
sources.note: Dates of the sea's retreat (1960s start, 1987 split, 2003 South Aral split, mid-2001 peninsula, 2004 17,160 km2, 2007 10%) used to read the small steps in the Cliopatria shapes of 2000 and 2006.

notes: Republic of Uzbekistan, five Cliopatria shapes 1992-2024 (414,068 to 415,143 km2), start moved to 31 August 1991 with a new 1991 keyframe. The five shapes are one frontier: on the grid 1992 equals 1996, 2000 adds one cell and 2006 adds five, all on the Aral Sea shore of Karakalpakstan, and 2024 equals 2006; no frontier moved on the grid. Uzbekistan's real changes are smaller than a cell: Bagys to Kazakhstan (2002, 517 ha exchange; matched by kazakhstan's 2002 gain), 156 km2 to Kyrgyzstan (17 November 2022; the kyrgyzstan dossier has no matching gain), the Kyrgyz enclave of Barak ending in 2024. Not opened (page budget 5 reached): Karakalpakstan (autonomy; the Uzbekistan page does not cover it), the Turkmenistan–Uzbekistan border, the Tajik civil war and the Batken/IMU incursions of 1999-2000, the Afghan fronts (Dostum, Termez) of 1996-2001; no war is listed for that reason. The Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan page says the Uzbek enclave of Jangail in Kyrgyzstan existed 'until 2026', beyond this dossier's 2024 end. Mismatch kept: Cliopatria draws 35 grid cells beyond Natural Earth's Uzbek line (17 in Kazakhstan) and omits about 146 inside it. The end year is 2024 as in the neighbouring dossiers (Cliopatria's last year). Names the gazetteer lacks: Bagys (place, Turkestan region of Kazakhstan); the lake name 'Aral Sea' resolves only as North Aral Sea or South Aral Sea.
